reasoning: The arithmetic bug is real. In ZAIWireTypes.swift:180-189, entries that are each > 0 are summed with no finiteness check, so two usage values of 1e308 give an infinite total, the share becomes inf/inf = NaN, and VendorSectionView.swift:638 calls Int() on it. But the attacker source is not established. The JSON comes only from a hardcoded endpoint: ZAIProvider.swift:10 is `URL(string: "https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit")`, which is not user-configurable. Nothing is on the path except the first-party vendor over TLS, and the config also has a pin_hosts option (AppConfig.swift:124). To send 1e308 values, an attacker would have to be Z.AI or OpenRouter themselves, or break TLS. The finding's only precondition is 'Attacker-controlled response', with no path that gets there. The cached copy of the payload sits in the user's own 0700 Application Support directory, so tampering with it requires the same user account, which is not an attacker boundary. flexibleDoubleIfPresent (AppConfig.swift:199-203) does accept any finite Double, so the robustness bug (a crash if the vendor sends absurd values) is worth fixing with a clamp, but it is not reachable by an attacker as written.
